questions.question: Which muscle arises from the upper three-fourth of the anterior surface of the ulna?
questions.explanation: The flexor digitorum profundus arises from the upper three-fourth of the anterior surface.

questions.question: The pronator quadratus arises from an oblique ridge on which part of the anterior surface?
questions.explanation: The pronator quadratus arises from an oblique ridge on the lower one-fourth of the anterior surface.

questions.question: Which direction does the nutrient foramen on the anterior surface of the ulna face?
questions.explanation: The nutrient foramen is located a little above the middle of the anterior surface and is directed upwards.

questions.question: From which part of the medial surface does the flexor digitorum profundus arise?
questions.explanation: The flexor digitorum profundus arises from the upper two-third of the medial surface.

questions.question: What structure divides the posterior surface of the ulna into upper and lower parts?
questions.explanation: An oblique line divides the posterior surface into a smaller upper part and a large lower part.

questions.question: Which muscle inserts on the area above the oblique line on the posterior surface?
questions.explanation: The area above the oblique line on the posterior surface receives the insertion of the anconeus muscle.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the upper one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line?
questions.explanation: The lateral part below the oblique line provides attachment to the abductor pollicis longus in its upper one-fourth.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the middle one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line?
questions.explanation: The middle one-fourth of the lateral part provides attachment to the extensor pollicis longus.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the third one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line?
questions.explanation: Extensor indicis attaches to the next one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line.

questions.question: The distal one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line is characterized by which feature?
questions.explanation: The distal one-fourth of the lateral part below the oblique line is devoid of any attachments.

questions.question: The convex articular surface on the lateral side of the ulnar head forms which joint?
questions.explanation: The convex articular surface on the lateral side of the ulnar head articulates with the radius to form the inferior radio-ulnar joint.

questions.question: What separates the inferior surface of the ulnar head from the wrist joint?
questions.explanation: The inferior surface of the ulnar head is separated from the wrist joint by an articular disc of the inferior radio-ulnar joint.

questions.question: From which aspect of the ulnar head does the styloid process project downwards?
questions.explanation: The styloid process projects downwards from the posteromedial aspect of the head of the ulna.

questions.question: Which structure attaches to the tip of the ulnar styloid process?
questions.explanation: The tip of the ulnar styloid process provides attachment to the medial collateral ligament of the wrist joint.

questions.question: Which tendon lies in the groove between the back of the ulnar head and the styloid process?
questions.explanation: The tendon of extensor carpi ulnaris lies in the groove between the back of the head of the ulna and the styloid process.

questions.question: The ulnar styloid process can be palpated when the forearm is in which position?
questions.explanation: The styloid process may be felt slightly distal to the head when the forearm is pronated.

questions.question: When the elbow is fully extended, where do the olecranon process and the epicondyles lie?
questions.explanation: When the elbow is fully extended, the tip of the olecranon process and the epicondyles lie in the same horizontal line.

questions.question: When the elbow is fully flexed, what shape is formed by the three bony points?
questions.explanation: When fully flexed, the olecranon process and the two epicondyles form an equilateral triangle.

questions.question: A fracture of the upper third of the ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head is termed what?
questions.explanation: This specific combination of injuries is called a Monteggia fracture dislocation.

questions.question: Which fracture involves the lower third of the radial shaft and dislocation of the inferior radio-ulnar joint?
questions.explanation: A fracture of the lower third of the radius with inferior radio-ulnar joint dislocation is a Galeazzi fracture dislocation.

questions.question: A direct injury to the ulnar shaft caused by raising the forearm to ward off a blow is called what?
questions.explanation: This mechanism of injury results in a night-stick fracture.

questions.question: How many primary and secondary ossification centers does the ulna have in total?
questions.explanation: The ulna ossifies from three centers: one primary for the shaft and two secondary for the ends.

questions.question: During which week of intrauterine life does the primary ossification center appear?
questions.explanation: The primary center appears in the mid-shaft during the eighth week of intrauterine life.

questions.question: At what age does the secondary center for the upper end of the ulna appear?
questions.explanation: The secondary center for the upper end appears at 9 years.

questions.question: At what age does the secondary center for the upper end of the ulna fuse?
questions.explanation: The upper end secondary center fuses at 18 years.

questions.question: At what age does the secondary center for the lower end of the ulna appear?
questions.explanation: The lower end (middle of head) center appears at 6 years.

questions.question: At what age does the secondary center for the lower end of the ulna fuse?
questions.explanation: The lower end center fuses at 20 years.

questions.question: How is the distal part of the olecranon process formed?
questions.explanation: The distal part of the olecranon process is formed as an upward extension of the shaft.

questions.question: Which structure stabilizes the forearm by gripping the lower end of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The ulna stabilizes the forearm by gripping the lower end of the humerus by its trochlear notch.

questions.question: Which bone provides the foundation for the radius to produce supination and pronation?
questions.explanation: The ulna provides the foundation for the radius to produce supination and pronation at the radio-ulnar joints.
